sentences.text: The genus name Niobrarasaurus was chosen to honor the Niobrara Formation where the fossils were found.
The remains were discovered in Gove County, about 11 miles south of Hackberry, Kansas, approximately 195 feet above the base of the Niobrara Formation.

The dinosaur lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, between 87 and 83 million years ago, during the Coniacian and Santonian stages, while the fossil record indicates a time range from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
The habitat was near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous.
It is debated whether Hierosaurus coleii should be considered a distinct genus or a synonym of Nodosaurus, leading to its reclassification as Niobrarasaurus.
